data.name: Meghraj
data.gender_notes: Meghraj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Meghraj is the name of the god of clouds in Hindu mythology. He is also known as Indra's chariot, as he is believed to transport Indra, the god of rain, across the sky. The name Meghraj carries the meaning “God of Clouds” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Meghraj usually hope their child will grow to embody god of clouds and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of rain and fertility.
data.etymology: Meghraj belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Clouds.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Meghraj total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Meghraj is a name deeply rooted in Hindu culture, representing the divine power of the monsoon rains and the gift of life-giving water. In various Hindu art forms, Meghraj is depicted as a majestic cloud with flowing drapes, underscoring his significant role in providing sustenance and prosperity to the land.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Meghraj represents the divine essence of cloud, which is an embodiment of joy and abundance. Meghraj holds a purifying influence, both figuratively and literally, as a cloud cleanses the air and seals the wounds of a parched earth. Additionally, as an avatar of Indra, Meghraj symbolizes the power to bring change and transformation through the forces of nature.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Meghraj: Ruler of the clouds. In Hindu mythology, Meghraj is the king of the clouds and is believed to shower blessings of rain. The name signifies the power to bring nourishment and prosperity through the monsoons.

vedic_reference.note: Meghraj is a name derived from Sanskrit roots, referring to the cloud king or sky ruler.

historical_references.reference: Meghraj was the name of a famous Jain Tirthankara, who is believed to have lived around the 11th or 12th century BC during the Aras or Nabhakalpa era.

Meghraj is also the name of a celestial god in Hindu mythology, who is believed to be the ruler of the rain clouds and the god of rain. He is often depicted as riding a white elephant and holding an umbrella.
